text:
sasha_support: ftw-corp is seeing intermittent 429s in prod since 11:42 UTC. Only on /v1/chat/stream. Customer says it spikes for ~10s at minute boundaries. They included one response header: 
  HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
  Retry-After: 1
  x-rate-limit-limit: 600 RPM
  x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
  x-rate-limit-reset: 167

sasha_support: they say they send ~8k req/min but mostly steady except these microbursts. Asking if this is an RPM vs TPM alignment issue or something on our side. I've asked for a customer request-id but haven't got it yet.

ryan_oncall: @sasha_support ok — first checks: get the exact x-* headers for one of the failed requests (full set), and the request-id header from our gateway (x-rw-request-id or request-id). also confirm whether they're using HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 multiplexing and whether streaming clients hold long-lived connections.

mina_infra: Also need their client concurrency and whether they do parallel streaming (multiple streams per auth token). If they're multiplexing HTTP/2 a lot, per-connection slotting can cause burst collapse into a few seconds. Do we have their account id?

sasha_support: account id 98765-corp. customer says Node SDK v2.3, streaming = true, they use up to 120 concurrent streams from a handful of hosts. Attached snippet from them: 

  --- customer log ---
  [2026-03-15T11:42:12Z] request_id=rw:abc123 status=429 route=/v1/chat/stream headers="Retry-After:1 x-rate-limit-remaining:0 x-rate-limit-reset:167"
  [2026-03-15T11:42:12Z] client_conns=28 concurrent_streams=120
  [2026-03-15T11:42:18Z] request_id=rw:abc124 status=200 route=/v1/chat/stream
  --- end ---

sasha_support: they also said they didn't change code or deploy around that time.

mina_infra: quick hypothesis: their request bursts are aligning to minute boundaries and exhausting the per-minute token bucket (RPM). With streaming concurrency, their 120 parallel streams may fan-in on refill boundaries and briefly exceed the bucket even if average RPM is within quota. TPM (tokens per minute per route) vs TTL matters. Ask them to check if they batch new streams at fixed cron seconds (e.g., every 00s) — jittering start times usually fixes it.

ryan_oncall: run this to pull our side logs for the window (internal): 
  rcli logs query --account 98765-corp --from 2026-03-15T11:42:00Z --to 2026-03-15T11:43:00Z --filter "status:429" --fields request_id,timestamp,route,client_ip,az,model

mina_infra: mitigation guidance to give customer now: 
  - add jitter to stream startup (random 0-10s) to avoid minute-boundary stampede
  - cap concurrent streams per host (try 10-20) rather than 120 one-shot
  - honor Retry-After and implement exponential backoff with jitter, not fixed tight loops
  - prefer batching requests where possible, or switch to embed+batch flow if applicable
  - check SDK version and enable client-side token folding (v2.4 has smarter refill)

mina_infra: also ask support to check their per-route quotas in admin console — some accounts have conservative default RPM and TPM for streaming routes. If they need steady high throughput, recommend Dedicated capacity or quota bump.

sasha_support: ran rcli (output excerpt): 
  rw:abc123 2026-03-15T11:42:12Z /v1/chat/stream 429 us-east-1 10.1.2.3 model=redwood-large
  rw:abc125 2026-03-15T11:42:12Z /v1/chat/stream 429 us-east-1 10.1.2.4 model=redwood-large
  rw:abc126 2026-03-15T11:42:13Z /v1/chat/stream 429 us-east-1 10.1.2.5 model=redwood-large
  rw:abc124 2026-03-15T11:42:18Z /v1/chat/stream 200 us-east-1 10.1.2.3 model=redwood-large

sasha_support: deploy-bot shows a routine infra rollout at 11:41:50 but no errors in the deploy message.

deploy-bot: Deploy notice: rollout service=ingress-proxy az=us-east-1 id=deploy-20260315-041. No errors.

mina_infra: that pattern (3–5 429s at 11:42:12 then normal responses) matches a refill-boundary stampede. We should confirm the customer's # of API keys per region (multiple tokens can increase effective parallelism). Also check if they split requests across multiple endpoints/azs — uneven routing can concentrate traffic.

ryan_oncall: next steps: 
  1) ask customer for an example request-id from a failure (one of rw:abc123 style) and last 5 min sample client logs
  2) ask them to temporarily limit concurrent streams to 20 and add 0-7s jitter and see if spikes stop
  3) we'll run a short simulated replay from our test harness (match their concurrency/seq) to confirm server-side throttling behavior
  4) if confirmed, offer an immediate short-term quota bump or suggest Dedicated capacity depending on their expected sustained TPS

sasha_support: pinging customer with steps and asking for request-ids. I'll run the rcli replay once they give permission.

mina_infra: note for runbook: consider adding a diagnostic flag to include x-rw-request-id in SDK client logs and a heartbeat metric exposing per-second token burn. That would make these incidents faster to triage.

ryan_oncall: +1 to runbook item. tagging eng:infra to follow up on metrics.

sasha_support: thanks all — will update thread when customer responds. :thumbsup:
